stomach-hacking hunger, sunlight, the constant itch of blight which seeped into far too many people and clung like HIV but twinging happily in the brain. it was a disgrace to marlins old badge from the marines. and, if the marines still existed as more then a shattered fraternity, that badge would have been worth something. he wiped a layer of sand off his robes.

the convoy had been on a circling patrol across the gulf of sand that used to coastal waters off California, for years now. it was tedious, it tested their daily loyalty and many often failed. the five infantry and two tanks that remained now, had used to be part of the entire California garrison, but when the new raiders came seeping in with the gold advantage of being vaccinated against the blight, most of the garrison was already fighting their brothers in arms.

he almost couldn't remember if the government had stopped talking to them at that point. the lead tank suddenly halted, the commander popping open the hatch. "maggots, over here, now." he barked. even from marlins distance the red drawn eyes of a blight sufferer were obvious. when all of them had clustered, the briefing came out, as the convoys UAV perched on the tanks hull.

"five miles north, aiming for the mariners arch. the bots pinged them having a red cross symbol, and given their size, its likely only medical supplies" the commander explained. the red crosses protection had begun to fall quite early, marlin mused. but he and the others checked their guns, one of the infantrymen was already out of ammo, but that was, eh.

they began the march north, the UAV lifted off to cover the area. it was an age to ration your food, it was an age to eat the weak, it was an age to rob the doctors, and prowl your territory, and this was just another day.
